b1-21-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Giving Your Opinion
b1-21-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about the city's proposal to close the centre of Budapest to cars on Sundays. You like it, and you have a reason.
b1-21-01.prompt: Tell Carlos your opinion about the proposal and give a reason.
cues: Say what you think of the proposal
b1-21-01.target: Me parece que la propuesta es razonable porque ayuda a muchas personas.
b1-21-01.english: It seems to me that the proposal is reasonable because it helps many people.
b1-21-01.canDo: I can express an opinion and give a reason.

b1-21-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Agreeing, But...
b1-21-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg likes the Sunday proposal for the centre of Budapest. You agree with it, but you think it needs some changes.
b1-21-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you agree, but that the proposal needs changes.
cues: Say what you think it needs
b1-21-02.target: Estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta, pero creo que necesita algunos cambios.
b1-21-02.english: I agree with the proposal, but I think it needs some changes.
b1-21-02.canDo: I can agree partly and disagree respectfully.

b1-21-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What a Good Debate Needs
b1-21-03.scenario: You are Meg. Your class at the university in Budapest is preparing a debate, and Carlos asks what is important for it to go well.
b1-21-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is important and what is necessary for a good debate.
b1-21-03.target: Es importante que escuchemos opiniones diferentes. Es necesario que consideremos la evidencia.
b1-21-03.english: It is important that we listen to different opinions. It is necessary that we consider the evidence.
b1-21-03.canDo: I can evaluate ideas and discuss what is necessary.

b1-21-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Backing Up a View
b1-21-04.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest your team compares two plans. Meg asks which one you support and why.
b1-21-04.prompt: Tell Meg which plan you support, why, and how the other plan differs.
cues: Say which plan you support and why
Say how the other plan is different
b1-21-04.target: Apoyo la primera propuesta porque es más sencilla. En cambio, la segunda tendría más costes.
b1-21-04.english: I support the first proposal because it is simpler. By contrast, the second would have more costs.
b1-21-04.canDo: I can support opinions with reasons and evidence.

b1-21-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short Essay on Opinions
b1-21-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a short essay in the style of the Paliques by Clarín for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what the writer says.
b1-21-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what many people do and what the writer asks of them.
b1-21-05.target: Muchas personas dan su opinión sin pensarlo antes. La persona que escribe pide que reconozcan lo que saben y lo que no saben.
b1-21-05.english: Many people give their opinion without thinking first. The writer asks them to recognise what they know and what they do not know.
b1-21-05.canDo: I can take part in a sustained debate.

b1-21-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Condition and a Conclusion
b1-21-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks whether you support the Sunday proposal after all. You see some limitations, but you have a condition.
b1-21-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg your conclusion about the proposal and your condition.
cues: Give your conclusion and a condition
b1-21-consolidation.target: Aunque tiene algunas limitaciones, la propuesta es útil. Apoyo la medida siempre que ayude a todos.
b1-21-consolidation.english: Although it has some limitations, the proposal is useful. I support the measure as long as it helps everyone.
b1-21-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate opinion and debate vocabulary.
